hypothesis.text: Modify the embedded-VNS decision in `scheduler.py` to use a deterministic value-of-polish gate: always polish the initial incumbent as today, but during ALNS invoke full VNS only for repaired candidates that improve the current or best pre-polish cost, plus a sparse exploration cadence; skip it for clearly worse candidates unless a configurable minimum exploration interval is due. Track recent VNS elapsed time and direct pre/post-polish distance reduction already available at the objective-probe boundary, and thin the exploration cadence when recent polishing has no positive reduction or consumes a disproportionate runtime share. The gate changes only which feasible candidate is locally searched; destroy/repair, capacity validation, customer coverage, route-limit rejection, SA acceptance, deadline reserve, and the external `solve` contract remain unchanged. This should preserve fleet_violation while reallocating budget from low-value polishing to more ALNS iterations and selectively polishing promising candidates, improving final paired total_distance among equal-fleet feasible outputs.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The champion runs the full, exhaustive embedded VNS after virtually every repaired ALNS candidate (`EMBEDDED_VNS_CADENCE = 1`). Since VNS includes repeated cross-route neighborhoods, this can consume most of the fixed budget polishing candidates that will later be rejected, reducing the number and diversity of destroy/repair trajectories explored.
hypothesis.expected_effect: On instances where every-iteration VNS dominates runtime, increase completed ALNS iterations and accepted high-quality candidates while retaining direct VNS improvements on promising repairs; target a lower final total_distance with no increase in fleet_violation or structural failures.

hypothesis.text: Change the embedded-VNS policy defaults from unconditional every-iteration polishing to a bounded-runtime adaptive schedule: set a positive embedded-VNS runtime-share ceiling and a sparse positive cadence, while retaining the existing repair-improvement rescue. The scheduler already measures cumulative embedded-VNS time and, once the ceiling is reached, still runs VNS for candidates whose repaired state improves current or best cost. This reallocates time from polishing clearly unpromising candidates to generating more ALNS destroy/repair trajectories, but preserves intensive local search at the causal points most likely to yield a new incumbent. It does not alter route representation, capacity checks, customer coverage, or the scheduler's route-limit rejection, so fleet_violation remains protected before assessing total_distance.
hypothesis.target_weakness: For every instance at or below the VNS threshold, the default scheduler invokes the full seven-neighborhood embedded VNS after every ALNS destroy/repair iteration (`EMBEDDED_VNS_CADENCE = 1`) with no runtime-share cap. Under the budget-exhausting runtime model, this can repeatedly polish transient candidates and starve adaptive destroy/repair selection and acceptance of iterations needed for diversification.
hypothesis.expected_effect: On feasible equal-fleet outcomes, increase ALNS iteration throughput and incumbent opportunities, reducing final total_distance; validate first that fleet_violation never regresses, then compare paired final distance and runtime.

hypothesis.text: Add a bounded first-improvement inter-route 2-for-1 exchange neighborhood to the default VNS: enumerate an adjacent two-customer segment in a source route and one customer in a distinct destination route, test both orientations of the segment, and commit only if both resulting route loads respect capacity and the combined route-distance delta is strictly improving. Recalculate both routes, remove any empty route, and rebuild the solution index after an accepted move; poll the existing reserve deadline within enumeration exactly as the other neighborhoods do. This complements existing relocate, swap, Or-opt, and two-opt-star moves by permitting capacity rebalancing plus a coordinated geometric reassignment that those operators cannot express in one improving transition. Because every committed state preserves exact customer coverage, implicit-depot route structure, and capacity, it does not trade fleet_violation for distance; it should reduce final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible solutions, particularly after regret repair has created cross-route packing local minima.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The VNS can relocate only one customer, swap only one-for-one customers, or exchange route tails. It therefore cannot make a capacity-feasible two-customer-for-one-customer reassignment, leaving common tight-capacity cross-route local minima unresolved after destroy/repair and before ALNS acceptance.
hypothesis.expected_effect: More strictly improving feasible cross-route transitions during VNS and lower final paired total_distance without increasing fleet_violation or structural infeasibility.

hypothesis.text: Change the embedded-VNS defaults from unconditional every-iteration polishing to a bounded intensification schedule: retain initial VNS, run embedded VNS for a short early bootstrap, then use a sparse fixed cadence plus the existing repair-improvement rescue trigger, with a nonzero maximum embedded-VNS runtime share. The scheduler already measures ALNS elapsed time and cumulative VNS runtime and preserves rescue when repaired candidates improve the incumbent or best, so this change reallocates time from low-value polishing of clearly noncompetitive candidates to additional feasible ALNS destroy/repair attempts while still intensifying promising states. It changes neither route construction nor acceptance feasibility checks: capacity, unique coverage, and the route cap remain enforced before acceptance, preserving fleet_violation as the primary objective.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The default `EMBEDDED_VNS_CADENCE = 1` invokes a full seven-neighborhood, first-improvement VNS after every repaired ALNS candidate. Because VNS itself repeats neighborhoods until no improvement, this can consume most of a budget-exhausting run polishing candidates that are ultimately rejected, leaving too few independent destroy/repair trajectories for adaptive weights and simulated annealing to discover better route assignments.
hypothesis.expected_effect: On equal-fleet feasible runs, more ALNS iterations and operator samples should improve final total_distance; the runtime-share cap should reduce excessive embedded-VNS time without increasing hard infeasibility or fleet violation.
